By implementation of an appropriate maintenance program for the project, except for normal maintenance, shut down of facilities would seldom take place. Major maintenance would be scheduled when the facilities could be shut down without serious effects on system capacity and therefore should have little effect on system service.
Maintaining rights-of-way clearances would require that all tree tops be 30 feet below the conductors. This would mean a continuing loss of timber from these trees as long as the transmission line is used. Also, all vegetation would be cleared from around the towers, and thus, timber from these areas would also be lost for lumber production during the use of the transmission line.
Periodic selective cutting would create a greater diversity of wildlife habitat along the right-of-way and maintain early plant succession suitable for ruffed grouse, along with openings beneficial to deer, cottontail rabbit, bobwhite quail, and other species. Such maintenance procedures could have an adverse effect on wildlife species dependent on mature forest habitats.
3.3 TERMINATION AND ABANDONMENT
The Applicant's methods which might be used in the event of termination and/or abandonment of the proposed project have not been formulated. Basically, the way the project would be constructed would allow for the area to be returned almost to a natural state after abandonment. The plant could be dismantled and machinery removed. The entrances to the tunnel could be sealed and the dams could be removed and material from the dams returned to the borrow areas. However, these events are not considered practical. The lands would eventually return to the local climax species. Until the drained reservoir was stabilized by vegetation, erosion would be rapid and the streams would probably carry a heavy silt load. Visual evidence of the project would exist for many years unless all project structures were intentionally removed.
The upper reservoir could be utilized for fishing and other recreational uses after the addition of minor flood control works. The area could then be reforested with appropriate vegetation.
